newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent steady at lower levels after APIs, Iraq.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent steady at lower levels after APIs, Iraq.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures were steady at lower levels on Wednesday following the release of bearish U.S. inventory data and fresh reports from Iraq, traders and brokers said.
August Brent was 18 cents a barrel lower at 1150 GMT and was trading at $18.20, while July gas oil was unchanged at $162.75 a tonne.
"We are just bouncing off the lows," one broker said. "We are down because of the APIs and Iraq."
The American Petroleum Institute (API) said gasoline stocks fell by just 137,000 barrels last week, well below analysts' expectations.
Crude stocks jumped by 4.7 million barrels against earlier expectations of a crude draw.

The U.N. coordinator in Iraq said on Wednesday the world body had received the preliminary draft of the country's distribution and procurement plans, but that further meetings were needed to fill in some gaps in the draft.
Iraq's delay in submitting the plan had stalled the resumption of oil exports under the U.N.'s oil-for-food deal with Baghdad.
Technical analysts said they saw support for Brent at $18.08 and $17.97, while resistance would begin at $18.24-$18.28, then at $18.42. -- London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
